test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: At what rate of interest (in percentage) per year will a sum of money double itself in 5 years on simple interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any sum of money to **double** itself (n = 2) at **Simple Interest**, the **Interest** must be equal to the **Principal**.

Shortcut formula: **Rate (R) = 100 ÷ Time (T)**

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 5 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = **5 years**

Let **Principal (P)** = ₹100

Since the money doubles, **Amount (A)** = 2 × 100 = **₹200**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = **Amount (A) − Principal (P)**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5446fb4813a4971feb7245cfaa388abd4975e9c3598f1062a6632b299996b543.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = 200 − 100 = 100

⇒ 100 = (100 × R × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 5 × R

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ R = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of money n-times itself

If a sum becomes n-times itself in T years at SI, then **R = 100(n − 1) ÷ T**.

Compound Interest Doubling (Rule of 72)

To find the approximate time to double money at CI, use **T ≈ 72 ÷ R**.

Difference between SI and CI

Difference for 2 years = **P(R ÷ 100)²**.

24
